Revised assessment: The tone is mildly positive—solid job gains and strong household spending—tempered by weak business fixed investment and below-target inflation. In line with investment-driven views of the cycle (where investment fluctuations account for much of output variability) and New Keynesian stabilization principles linking inflation and the output gap (e.g., Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido), the 25 bp cut and balance-sheet operations (T-bill purchases and repo facilities) reinforce the liquidity effect and support transmission by maintaining ample reserves (B. Friedman; McCallum and Nelson). With market-based inflation compensation low and expectations central to inflation dynamics (Svensson; Cagan-style expectations), a Taylor-rule-style reaction—easing when inflation is below the symmetric 2% objective despite tight labor markets—justifies the cautious, supportive stance. Overall, the communication is supportive but not exuberant.
